title: The quality management approach in agile
blurb: Say what the quality management approach covers in an agile project, and tell it apart from the other approaches and registers.
question: A supplier will test its software with automated test-first methods, and the board wants the team's agile behaviours assured. Where should both be documented?

teach.body: The quality management approach describes the quality techniques and standards to be applied, and the roles and responsibilities for achieving the required quality specifications and acceptance criteria. In plain English: it is the agreed rulebook for HOW quality will be achieved and checked on this project. It is one of the management approaches agreed in initiation and held in the PID.

teach.h: The agile twist: ways of working are assured too
teach.body: PRINCE2 Agile adds something important. Agile ways of working should be built into the quality management approach and documented there, so that agile behaviours are part of the approach and are properly assured. The approach is also where the project records the agile testing methods it will use, including those of external suppliers.

teach.h: What goes into the quality management approach
head: Content
Agile example
rows: Accessibility or brand standards to meet
Who tests, who reviews, who accepts
Behaviours to be documented and assured
Shown or linked in the project backlog
teach.caption: The project backlog shows or links the project DoR and DoD taken from the quality management approach (8.3.2.1).

teach.h: When it is created and agreed
Three approaches that get mixed up

teach.body: Corvane Insurance is building a claims portal with an external developer, Bluefen Digital. During initiation, project manager Hannah Okafor runs the project initiation workshop. The quality management approach records Bluefen's automated test-first method, the accessibility standard, who tests and who accepts, and the team's agreed agile behaviours so project assurance can check them. Corvane's own release procedure replaces the standard one, recorded as a tailoring decision in the PID.

teach.text: The quality management approach says HOW quality will be achieved (techniques, standards, roles, agile ways of working). The quality register records WHAT quality activities were planned and done. Agile behaviours belong in the quality management approach, not in the communication management approach or the lessons log.

teach.body: If the business has its own product design, development and testing procedures that have worked well, the project may use them. There is no need to change supplier or rewrite them. The decision is documented as part of the tailoring decisions in the PID, which keeps it visible to the board and to assurance.

items: Describes quality techniques, standards, and roles and responsibilities (Table 9.1).
Agile ways of working are built in and documented so agile behaviours are assured.
Records agile testing methods, including external suppliers' methods.
Source of the project DoR and DoD, which the project backlog shows or links.
Agreed in initiating a project; co-created in the project initiation workshop; held in the PID.
Own procedures may be used: record that as a tailoring decision in the PID.

summary: You can now say what the quality management approach covers in an agile project, including agile ways of working and suppliers' testing methods. You can also tell it apart from the communication and commercial management approaches and from the quality register.

A.q: What does the quality management approach describe?
options: Quality activities planned or done, with their pass or fail results
Quality techniques, standards, and roles and responsibilities
All products required by a plan and the status of each product
The means and frequency of communication with stakeholders
A.why: The quality management approach describes the quality techniques and standards to apply and the roles and responsibilities for achieving quality specifications and acceptance criteria (Table 9.1).

whyNot.0: Planned and completed quality activities with results are recorded in the quality register.
whyNot.2: Products and their status are listed in the product register.
whyNot.3: Communication means and frequency belong in the communication management approach.

A.q: Where should a project document the agile ways of working that need to be assured?
A.why: Agile ways of working are incorporated and documented in the quality management approach so that agile behaviours are part of it and properly assured (Table 9.1).

whyNot.0: The communication management approach covers how and how often the project communicates.
whyNot.1: The lessons log records lessons for this or future projects, not the agreed ways of working.
whyNot.2: The quality register records quality activities and results, not behaviours.

A.q: An external supplier will use its own automated testing methods. Where should these be documented?
A.why: Agile testing methods, including those used by external suppliers, are documented in the quality management approach (Table 9.1).

whyNot.1: The commercial management approach covers procurement and contracts, not the supplier's testing methods.
whyNot.2: The product register lists products and their status.
whyNot.3: The project canvas sets out the business justification on one page.

B.q: In which process is the quality management approach agreed?
B.why: The 'agree the management approaches' activity in initiating a project covers the quality management approach, among the others (Table 13.6).

whyNot.0: Starting up produces the project brief and project canvas, not the management approaches.
whyNot.1: Managing product delivery is where teams accept, execute and deliver work packages.
whyNot.3: Controlling a stage is day-to-day stage control after the approaches are in place.

B.q: A retailer's own design and testing procedure has worked well on past projects. What does PRINCE2 Agile suggest?
options: Use it and record a tailoring decision in the PID
Replace it with the standard procedure in full
Hire a second supplier to check it independently
Raise an exception report for the board to decide
B.why: An alternative procedure may be used when the business has its own design, development and testing procedures; record it as a tailoring decision in the PID (9.3.1).

whyNot.1: PRINCE2 Agile allows the organization's own procedure, so replacing it is not required.
whyNot.2: Nothing suggests a second supplier is needed; tailoring covers this choice.
whyNot.3: Exception reports are for forecasts beyond tolerance, not a choice of procedure.

B.q:
Which two statements about the quality management approach are correct?
1. It records each quality check and its pass or fail result.
2. It can include the agile testing methods of suppliers.
3. It is where agile behaviours are documented to be assured.
4. It replaces the project backlog as the source of requirements.
B.why: The approach records agile testing methods including suppliers' (2) and documents agile ways of working so behaviours are assured (3) (Table 9.1).

whyNot.0: Statement 1 is wrong: individual checks and results go in the quality register.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: results go in the quality register, and the project backlog stays the requirements source.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: the quality practice is driven by the requirements in the project backlog.

C.q: In the project initiation workshop, which topic co-creates the quality management approach, and in which process is that workshop held?
options: Project Definition of Done; managing a stage boundary
Persona definition; starting up a project
C.why: The 'management approaches' topic of the project initiation workshop co-creates the approaches, and the workshop supports initiating a project (Table 13.7).

whyNot.0: The project DoD topic sets acceptance criteria for work; the workshop is not part of a stage boundary.
whyNot.1: Persona definition describes typical users; the workshop belongs to initiation, not starting up.
whyNot.2: The Agilometer topic assesses agile risks; the workshop belongs to initiation, not directing.

C.q: Project assurance wants to check that the team's agreed agile behaviours are being followed. Which product sets them out, and where is it held?
C.why: Agile behaviours are documented in the quality management approach so they can be assured, and the management approaches are held in the PID (Table 9.1, Table 13.6).

whyNot.0: The lessons log records lessons learned, not the agreed behaviours to be assured.
whyNot.1: A team charter is not the PRINCE2 Agile product for assured behaviours, and the product backlog holds user stories.
whyNot.3: The communication management approach does not describe agile behaviours, and approaches are not held in the brief.

C.q: The project backlog shows the project Definition of Ready and Definition of Done. Where do these definitions come from, and who owns the project backlog?
options: The product register; the project manager
The quality management approach; the CPO
The team plan; the product owner
The project canvas; the project executive
C.why: The project backlog shows or links the project DoR and DoD from the quality management approach, and the chief product owner owns the project backlog (8.3.2.1, Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: The product register lists products and status; it is not the source of the DoR and DoD.
whyNot.2: The team plan is the iteration-level plan, and the PO owns a product backlog, not the project backlog.
whyNot.3: The project canvas is the business justification; the executive does not own the project backlog.

reteach.title: The rulebook and the scoresheet
reteach.question: How do you stop mixing up the quality management approach with the quality register?

blocks.body: Think of a football league. The rulebook says how matches are played, who referees and what counts as a goal: that is the quality management approach. The scoresheet records each match played and the result: that is the quality register. In agile, the rulebook also spells out how the teams are expected to work together, so referees (assurance) can check it.

blocks.text: If the question asks HOW quality will be achieved, or where agile behaviours or a supplier's testing method are recorded, choose the quality management approach.

explain.body: The approach sets out the quality techniques and standards to apply, and the roles and responsibilities for meeting quality specifications and acceptance criteria.

test.q: A board wants to know which standards the products must meet and who is responsible for checking them. Which product should it read?
test.why: Standards and the roles and responsibilities for quality are described in the quality management approach (Table 9.1).

whyNot.0: The quality register records quality activities and results, not the standards to apply.
whyNot.1: The product register lists products and their status.
whyNot.2: The communication management approach covers the means and frequency of communication.

explain.body: Agile ways of working are incorporated and documented in the approach, so that agile behaviours are part of it and properly assured.

test.q: Why does PRINCE2 Agile put agile ways of working into the quality management approach?
options: So the behaviours can be properly assured
So they replace the communication plan
So the board can set their tolerances
So suppliers can price them in contracts
test.why: Documenting agile ways of working in the quality management approach makes agile behaviours part of the approach and properly assured (Table 9.1).

whyNot.1: The communication management approach is a separate product with a different purpose.
whyNot.2: Tolerances apply to performance targets, not to behaviours.
whyNot.3: Contract matters sit in the commercial management approach.

explain.body: Suppliers' agile testing methods are written into the approach. If the business prefers its own design, development and testing procedure, that is allowed and recorded as a tailoring decision in the PID.

test.q: Where is the decision to use the organization's own testing procedure recorded?
test.why: Use of an alternative procedure is documented as part of the tailoring decisions in the PID (9.3.1).

whyNot.0: The quality register logs quality activities and results.
whyNot.1: The commercial management approach covers procurement and contracts.
whyNot.3: The product backlog holds user stories, not tailoring decisions.

explain.body: The approach is agreed in initiating a project, under 'agree the management approaches', and is co-created in the management approaches topic of the project initiation workshop.

test.q: Which workshop includes a topic for co-creating the management approaches?
test.why: The project initiation workshop has a 'management approaches' topic to co-create them (Table 13.7).

whyNot.0: The project canvas workshop builds the canvas: users, vision, benefits, scope, costs and so on.
whyNot.2: The team planning workshop prepares the next iteration.
whyNot.3: The release planning workshop updates OKRs and the release map at a stage boundary.
